title: Proprietary now; deliberate dependency and future licensing choices

nodes.summary: Kyyn-owned code is proprietary, all rights reserved, for now
nodes.detail: Kernel, SDK, first-party code and docs are all-rights-reserved during development: no permissive headers, no promise of redistribution rights, no claim of being open source. A future permissive release needs an explicit owner decision.

realised.evidence: The first Kyyn packages (PR 6) declare license NONE with an all-rights-reserved copyright; README states the project is proprietary

nodes.summary: Licensing policy never overrides third-party notices; distributed sources are reviewed
nodes.detail: The policy does not relicense copied code or rewrite existing notices. Every source actually shipped (native binaries, guest bundles, generated code, tools, web assets, including native-linked MicroHs modules) is reviewed, its notices preserved and local patches documented.

realised.evidence: PR 6 vendors MicroHs/json/transformers with a source, hash and license inventory (vendor/README.md); PR 8 adds docs/dependency-sources.md

nodes.summary: Plugin architecture independent of licensing; no signing or approval service
nodes.detail: External extensibility and the plugin authoring boundary do not depend on the licensing choice, and proprietary development implies no mandatory signing/approval service or plugin compatibility lock.

realised.evidence: Negative constraint; no code existed and no signing/approval service was ever introduced

nodes.summary: Dependencies chosen for current proprietary and possible future permissive release
nodes.detail: Dependency adoption considers both the proprietary policy and a possible permissive release; license questions are identified before adopting code and resolved explicitly (with legal review when unclear), never by silently changing policy or treating future open source as permission now.

realised.evidence: Dependency source/license records accompany adoption from PR 8 (docs/dependency-sources.md) onward; this is a process commitment, so evidence is indirect

nodes.summary: Guest JSON library choice gated on license terms plus compatibility proof
nodes.detail: The guest JSON library (Aeson vs microaeson candidates) stays unselected until its exact source/dependency terms are checked alongside the compatibility proof; API convenience alone does not approve it for a guest bundle.

realised.evidence: PR 5 retained source/license and compatibility evidence before the owner accepted the library choice

nodes.summary: Selected host/guest JSON libraries recorded in ADR 0007 with license evidence
nodes.detail: The JSON choice is now made (Aeson on the host, unchanged json-0.11 modules on MicroHs, owned by ADR 0007), with source/license evidence retained; the check of exact terms alongside the compatibility proof still applies to any change.

realised.evidence: PR 6 vendors json-0.11 with its BSD-3-Clause license recorded in vendor/README.md

editorial.note: Repoints license evidence from the deleted protocol investigation to the vendor inventory and dependency-sources docs
Metadata reconciliation: drops the Status preamble, whose content the Decision section already states

notes: A small, policy-only lane that barely moved: one substantive change (seq 5, the JSON library getting selected, with ownership handed to ADR 0007) and two documentation-housekeeping steps. Realisation is mostly about repository hygiene rather than code: the all-rights-reserved posture shows up as license: NONE plus an all-rights-reserved copyright in Kyyn-owned cabal files, and the vendor/ inventory records upstream licenses (MicroHs Apache-2.0, json/transformers BSD-3, agentic BSD-2). Worth watching: the vendor table notes MicroHs currently comes from the owner's fork with a GC fix, so the 'document local patches' rule is in active use. The founding Decision paragraph on third-party notices was merged into the source-review node because the dependency section restates it; 'Verification and later release' produced no node.
